title: Kotlin Multiplatform, from the compiler up
intro: Follow one Kotlin function through the Android and iOS builds. Then see what Swift can call, how memory and threads behave on iOS, and how Compose Multiplatform draws the UI.
how: Each puzzle starts with a problem shared code has to solve, gives you one building block, shows it in a diagram that plays itself, and ends with three questions you have to answer to unlock the next one. Facts come from Kotlin's own documentation, linked on every page.
heroAlt: Animated diagram: one Kotlin file goes through the compiler's front end and comes out as JVM bytecode for Android and native code for an iPhone.

modules.title: Module 1: One codebase, two worlds
modules.blurb: From one source file to two kinds of machine code, how Kotlin reaches Apple's code, what an iOS app is, and how Swift sees what you built.

modules.title: Module 2: Living on iOS
modules.blurb: How memory is freed on each side and where that breaks, the main thread on iOS, coroutines there, and shipping one framework.

modules.title: Module 3: Sharing the UI
modules.blurb: Compose from its one core idea, what Compose Multiplatform shares, and how it draws on iOS.

modules.title: Module 4: The build
modules.blurb: What the kotlin { } block declares, the tree of source sets between commonMain and each target, who can see what, where each library goes, what a klib holds, how one dependency line finds every target's file, and how platform code is handed in.

modules.title: Module 5: Kotlin/Native under the hood
modules.blurb: What happens after the klibs: the link stage and LLVM, the linker and dead code elimination, static or dynamic frameworks and embedding, XCFrameworks and where the files land, how Xcode runs Gradle, what has to match (Mac, Xcode, iOS version), reading a crash with a dSYM, and where build minutes and megabytes go.

upcoming.title: Module 6: Across the boundary
upcoming.topics: Reading the generated header; generics, sealed classes and enums in Swift; default arguments, overloads and names (@ObjCName, @HiddenFromObjC); exceptions as an error contract and Kotlin crashes in crash reports; suspend and Flow from Swift, threads and cancellation; SKIE and Swift export.

upcoming.title: Module 7: Shipping it to iOS
upcoming.topics: Shipping a framework to an iOS team that doesn't build Kotlin: Swift Package Manager with a binary XCFramework; CocoaPods; signing; the local and the released loop; versioning a shared module and its dSYMs; CI for Apple targets.

upcoming.title: Module 8: The common stack
upcoming.topics: Ktor's HttpClient and engines; kotlinx.serialization without reflection; SQLDelight; key-value settings; dependency injection with Koin across platforms; a ViewModel in commonMain; dates, files and bytes with kotlinx-datetime and kotlinx-io.

upcoming.title: Module 9: Testing shared code
upcoming.topics: commonTest and kotlin.test on every target; running tests on the iOS simulator; fakes instead of mocks; testing coroutines with runTest; testing the API Swift really sees.

upcoming.title: Module 10: Architecture and migrating an existing app
upcoming.topics: Where to draw the shared line; modules and one export module; migrating an Android app step by step; designing the API with the Swift team; memory and performance in production; crashes and logs from the field.

upcoming.title: Module 11: The expert's toolbox
upcoming.topics: cinterop for C and Objective-C libraries; compiler plugins and KSP in multiplatform; upgrading Kotlin safely; publishing your own multiplatform library; a capstone that ships one feature end to end.
